steps.what: Prepare the actual ethnographic question and field context, check existing access and participant permissions and identify what may actually be observed or recorded
inputs: Actual research question, field setting and existing permissions
outputs: Actual field plan and permitted recording scope

steps.what: Conduct actual ethnographic field participation, observation and participant conversations, respecting actual participant choices and the real setting
inputs: Actual field setting and participants within permitted scope
outputs: Actual observations, interactions and unresolved interpretive questions

steps.what: Write actual field notes and reflexive context, using existing note fields for verified date and field-session references while retaining description, meaning and uncertainty
inputs: Actual field observations and verified permitted session references
outputs: Actual contextual field notes with distinctions between observation and interpretation

steps.what: Save actual field notes in the same restricted research document location

tasks.design: Use existing restricted {DOCS} field-note templates to reuse verified session and date fields. Keep ethnographic participation, participant relationships, description and interpretation with the researcher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual field notes may repeat session metadata alongside substantive writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document fields can reduce that repeated entry without generating participant accounts.
tasks.still_hard: Ethnographic understanding depends on actual relationships, setting and reflexive interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise what an interaction means in context and what cannot responsibly be inferred.

ambition.what: Reduce actual repeated field-note metadata only.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: document fields can reuse verified session metadata; ethnographic field participation and contextual interpretation remain human work.

assumptions: Actual researcher produces the field observations in s2; s1 counts real planning and checking access/permission conditions and s3 counts actual descriptive and reflexive writing. No free recordings, transcripts, consent pack or pre-coded field data is assumed. Actual new access or participant permission work is retained in the real episode and not eliminated by a template.

S3 savings cover only verified date and permitted session references in an existing actual field note. Participant identities are not inferred or automatically copied. No model receives participant accounts or generates observations. Try existing document fields first; functionality already used earns no new benefit.

Field-note production is explicitly separated from participation before estimating a saving. No extra administrative report after every conversation is invented; these are actual research notes. Public release, data sharing or publication would need its own actual final-version authority and separate gated action.

Ordinary same-system save share1 represents negligible actual time, fully retained and ungated, with no saving or author self-approval. Shares are illustrative task effort independent of prompt priors, not measured research time.
unknowns: Which metadata is actually repeated manually in current field notes?
Which session references may be reused under the real recording permissions?
research_questions: Observe actual field-note production and distinguish substantive description from repeated permitted metadata without accessing unnecessary participant details.

already_counted.description: Actual field planning, participation, retained descriptive/reflexive note writing and ordinary save remain in s1-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain permitted session-reference fields beyond retained field-specific checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:24*.10=2.4 repeated session-field points less.5 upkeep=1.9. Low: recording permissions require session references to be manually selected or pseudonymised each time, leaving all24 note points human and no useful new field configuration or upkeep. All15 planning,60 fieldwork and1 save points remain. A permission-specific reference-reuse case, unmeasured.

tasks.short: Supervise student teaching, internship and research work

steps.what: Find the actual student's current teaching, internship or research plan, objectives and submitted work through native student and project views
inputs: Actual student identity, current objectives and existing submitted work
outputs: Verified supervision context and original work

steps.what: Read or observe the actual student work and assess progress, methods, ethical questions and the help the student needs
inputs: Actual original student work and verified objectives

steps.what: Supervise the actual student through discussion, observation and tailored feedback, agreeing practical next work and resolving questions
inputs: Actual supervisory assessment, student work and real student questions
outputs: Actual feedback, agreed next steps and unresolved issues

steps.what: Write the actual existing supervision entry after the meeting, using native student and project fields while retaining specific feedback and agreed work
inputs: Actual completed supervision and verified student/project identifiers
outputs: Actual supervision entry with feedback and agreed work

steps.what: Save the completed entry in the same supervision record

tasks.design: Use {LMS} and {DOCS} views to find actual student work and reuse checked student/project identifiers in the existing supervision entry. The teacher reads the work, supervises the student and writes the actual tailored feedback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual objectives and submissions may require separate navigation and repeated identifiers.
tasks.enabler_now: Native student views and supervision fields can reduce that clerical effort.
tasks.still_hard: Progress and ethical or methodological issues require original work and direct supervision.
tasks.human_edge: Give feedback the particular student can act on.

ambition.what: Support actual supervision with less context and identifier work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: learning systems can filter existing student work and reuse identifiers while supervision and feedback remain human work.

assumptions: Representative actual supervision episode with an existing required supervision entry; no extra post-meeting report is invented. Actual students and programme staff produce work and objectives in their normal activities; s1 counts retrieval and identity checking, s2 actual reading or observation. No free prepared student assessment is assumed.

S4 splits actual record writing from conversation; its reduction covers identifier entry, not feedback meaning. Try native views and fields first; existing use has zero new gain. No AI grading, misconduct decision or competence judgement is proposed.

This episode ends with actual supervision and its internal entry, not a grade publication, placement approval, certification or written external recommendation. Real separate registry imports or formal sends must be represented if required, with actual final-version authority; none is hidden in saving.

Ordinary same-system save share1 is negligible, fully retained and ungated, with no saving or author self-approval. Shares are illustrative task work independent of prompt priors; actual course or supervision setup occurs at its real frequency.
unknowns: Are student work and objectives actually available in one native view?
Which supervision entry is actually required?
research_questions: Observe actual supervision and distinguish source navigation, original work review, conversation and required entry production.

already_counted.description: Actual context checking, original student work review, direct supervision, retained entry and ordinary save remain in s1-s5.

incremental.description: Maintain project and student links beyond retained supervision-specific checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:15*.20+14*.10=4.4 gross less1 upkeep=3.4. Low: internship work is held outside the learning-system view and still takes all15 retrieval points; checked student/project fields in the actual supervision entry still save1.4, less1 upkeep=.4. All25 original review,45 supervision and1 save points remain. A submission-location constraint, unmeasured.

tasks.short: Hold office hours to advise and assist students

steps.what: Find the actual student's relevant course requirements or academic context for the question raised during the scheduled office-hours session using native course views
inputs: Actual student question and existing course or academic references
outputs: Verified context for the actual advice question

steps.what: Advise and assist the actual student during regularly scheduled office hours, listening, explaining course or research issues and agreeing useful next steps
inputs: Actual student, question and verified references
outputs: Actual advice, assistance and unresolved questions

steps.what: Write the actual required advising entry for this case after the discussion, recording advice actually given and agreed next steps
inputs: Actual completed advising case and actual record requirement

steps.what: Save the completed advising entry in the same record

tasks.design: Use existing {LMS} and {DOCS} course views to find references for the actual office-hours question. The teacher listens, advises and writes any actual required advising entry; the ordinary save stays fully retained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the relevant course or academic requirement can interrupt the actual conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native course views can reduce that navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Useful advice depends on the actual student's question and circumstances.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the student's difficulty and explain a helpful next step.

ambition.what: Improve context access during existing office hours.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native course views can locate existing requirements; student advice remains a human conversation.

assumptions: Illustrative actual advising case during scheduled office hours where an existing case-record requirement applies. Do not invent a note after every ordinary student question or extrapolate this record mix to all office hours. S1 is actual case lookup, not termly scheduling or course setup charged to each meeting.

Actual course owners produce references in normal work and the actual student supplies the question; s1 counts finding and checking applicable references, s2 actual advice. No free prepared student profile or model-generated advice is assumed.

Required record writing is separated from conversation in s3. Check the native advising form first; without demonstrated repeated fields no reduction to the actual9-point entry is claimed. Existing course views already used have no new benefit.

No grade, admission, exception approval, written recommendation or external message is hidden in this case. Such actual decisions and sends need their real authority and distinct final-version action. Ordinary same-system save share1 is negligible, fully retained and ungated with no saving or self-approval. Shares are illustrative and independent of prompt priors.
unknowns: Which actual office-hours cases require an advising entry?
Can course views find the applicable version for the actual student's question?
research_questions: Observe office-hours cases and separate actual context lookup, advice and genuinely required record writing without adding administrative work.

already_counted.description: Actual case-context checking, advising, required entry and ordinary save remain in s1-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain course-reference links beyond retained case checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:10*.20=2 case-navigation points less.5 extra upkeep=1.5. Low: the student's applicable course-version requirements are not indexed and require manual tracing, retaining all10 lookup points; do not deploy an unhelpful view or incur its upkeep. All80 actual advice,9 required entry and1 save points remain. A course-version availability case, unmeasured.

tasks.short: Plan, evaluate and revise anthropology or archaeology curricula and course materials

steps.what: Read actual course content, learning outcomes, student work and existing evaluation evidence, checking versions, source scope and current teaching requirements
inputs: Actual course materials, student work and existing evaluation evidence

steps.what: Evaluate actual curriculum and teaching methods, choose justified changes and map the selected outcomes, topics, assessments and materials into the actual revision structure
inputs: Actual original course evidence and current disciplinary requirements
outputs: Actual curriculum revision decisions and explicit selected outcome/content mapping

steps.what: Populate the actual revision template's selected outcome, topic, assessment-reference and material fields from the teacher's explicit mapping
inputs: S2 actual selected revision mapping and s1 checked source identifiers
outputs: Revised course structure with explicit populated fields and missing-link exceptions

steps.what: Revise actual course explanations and instructional materials with a bounded wording helper using only the chosen changes and verified disciplinary sources
inputs: Actual selected curriculum changes, verified sources and populated structure
outputs: Revised actual explanatory course materials with source links

loop.purpose: Draft explanatory wording for actual chosen course changes
loop.input: Teacher-selected changes and verified source content
loop.output: Proposed explanations tied to supplied sources and outcomes
loop.check: Teacher checks disciplinary meaning, outcome fit and every source against originals
loop.stop: Reject unsupported concepts or sources and write manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Explanatory prose varies while fixed selected fields remain deterministic in s3

steps.what: Check the complete revised curriculum and course materials for actual learning progression, source accuracy, accessibility and alignment of methods and assessments and correct defects
inputs: Complete actual revised course package and original evidence
outputs: Checked actual revised curriculum and course materials

steps.what: Save the actual revised working course package in the same document system

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} to populate the teacher's actual selected curriculum fields and draft bounded explanations from verified sources. The teacher evaluates the actual evidence, chooses revisions and checks the complete revised package, using {LMS} originals for alignment checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual selected curriculum changes can require repeated structure entry and explanatory composition.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit field population is deterministic and a bounded helper can express already chosen teaching changes.
tasks.still_hard: Disciplinary accuracy and a coherent learning progression require teaching judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Choose material and methods that help students understand the subject and its uncertainties.

ambition.what: Reduce demonstrated repeated revision composition within actual curriculum work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: course templates can populate explicit selected fields and bounded drafting can suggest explanatory wording; curriculum decisions and complete disciplinary checks remain human work.

assumptions: Actual students and course staff produce existing work and evaluation evidence in normal activity; s1 counts original source retrieval and reading and s2 actual evaluation, curriculum choices and mapping. New surveys, evidence coding or research are not free inputs and must be counted if required.

S3 requires teacher-selected outcome ID, topic, assessment reference, material source and actual revision mapping. It does not choose educational content. Missing source or outcome fields remain manual. Try native course and document templates first; existing automatic population has no new runtime gain.

S4's loop assists expression, not learning-outcome or student evaluation decisions. Original-source and complete package checks remain in s4-s5. No student grading, automated misconduct detection or invented bibliography is proposed.

The deliverable is the actual revised working curriculum and materials. Formal programme adoption, operative assessment change, learner publication or written distribution requires its real independent authority after the complete final version and a separate gated action; none is hidden in ordinary saving.

Ordinary same-system save share1 is negligible, fully retained and ungated, with no author self-approval or saving. Shares are illustrative actual revision work independent of prompt priors; curriculum redesign is counted at its actual frequency, not per lesson or advising session.
unknowns: Which actual course fields are still populated manually?
How much explanatory revision is compatible with source-bound drafting?
What real authority governs any later programme adoption or publication?
research_questions: Observe an actual revision and separate original evidence reading, content choices, field population, prose composition and complete teaching checks.

already_counted.description: Actual evidence reading, curriculum decisions, retained explanatory revision and complete package checking plus ordinary save remain in s1, s2 and s4-s6.

incremental.description: Maintain curriculum field mappings and source-bound helper examples beyond retained per-revision disciplinary checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:15 actual field points+25*.40=10 prose points=25 gross less4 upkeep=21. Low: the native course template already covers all15 fixed-field points, and specialist explanatory language requires16 of25 prose points rather than15; only9 additional prose points save, less4 upkeep=5. Source20, content decisions25, complete check14 and save1 remain. A template-availability and discipline-specific wording case, not a uniform percentage cut; unmeasured.
